pr_title: SEO: og:image:alt and twitter:image:alt on every page
text:
Code Review verdict: APPROVED at 5736cabc.

Scope: 2 files, +92/-12, head metadata plus a CI guard. No visible copy, ids, hooks, dataLayer events or form fields are touched, so no CRO/BA ping.

src/_includes/base.njk
1. og:image:alt and twitter:image:alt are now always emitted, once each, from one socialImageAlt value. The old conditional blocks that could omit them are gone.
2. The precedence matches the stated spec: front-matter ogImageAlt, then posts as title plus ', from [the agency]', then site.ogImageAlt for /og-image.png, then the title. The title is used as-is if it already contains '[the agency]'; otherwise the same suffix is added.
3. Behavior change, intended: ogImageAlt now beats the brand card. Before, /og-image.png forced site.ogImageAlt even when front matter set an alt. That is only a change for pages that set both. The homepage keeps site.ogImageAlt as long as it has no ogImageAlt front matter.
4. The post title strip only fires when ' | [the agency]' occurs exactly once, at the end. A mid-title occurrence is left alone. Correct.
5. `| escape` on both tags is right. Nunjucks escape returns a safe string, so there is no double escaping with or without autoescape.

scripts/content-checks.sh
6. og_image_alt_check uses HTMLParser and counts exact property or name matches. og:image:width, og:image:height and og:image:alt don't count as og:image. Pages without og:image are skipped, and a parse error is reported as a failure line. It runs in both head mode and the full run. Head mode now exits 1 on either check failing and 0 otherwise, which is equivalent to before for head_check.

Non-blocking: a page with no title and no ogImageAlt would get the alt ', from [the agency]'. The guard counts tags but doesn't check for empty or odd values. Worth a later check that the alt doesn't start with a comma.

pr_title: CI: content-checks gate for llms post count/list drift
text:
APPROVED at fba7cb5de41bbd6af07df7c29c69ffd0bf3c4e5a.

This PR changes only scripts/content-checks.sh and adds an llms drift gate that fails the build job on any mismatch. Built posts are counted from _site/blog/<slug>/index.html exactly two levels deep, with page and category excluded, so the hub, pagination and category pages are not counted, and the selftest covers each of those cases. Post dates are read from the post-meta time element, which htmlDateString renders in the site timezone, so an offset like 2026-10-19T08:00:00-07:00 resolves to the correct day. The empty cases fail loudly: a missing blog directory, a post without a date, a missing llms file, a missing or repeated count or Last updated line, and an llms.txt with no dated posts are all errors. Missing, extra and duplicate slugs are all reported.

Non-blocking: Future-dated posts count as built, because Eleventy builds them by default. That matches how the open post PRs are written. A Pillar-style dated bullet in llms.txt would widen the window to the whole archive. The selftest is only run by content-checks.sh selftest, so consider calling it in CI.

CI on fba7cb5d: Build and grep _site and Strings, logos, hooks are green, and Browser checks was skipped. 2. WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide): the logo ticker gives keyboard users no way to pause it. It starts on its own (after the logos decode, or 4s at most) and loops with no end, at about 80s per cycle on desktop and 54s on mobile. Nothing inside the visible copy is focusable. Fix without adding a visible control: let Enter and Space on the viewport toggle data-paused, and make its accessible name say that, for example "Client logos, press Enter to pause". The still row by default and the reduced-motion gate are good. The aria-hidden duplicate copy is correct.

Keyboard handling (script.js 945-955):

- When html.reveal-all is set, the handler returns before preventDefault, so Space scrolls the page normally.

- The new screen-reader-only text is "Press Enter or Space to pause or resume." It is clean under house rules, and Copywriter should include it in the PASS at this head.

Scope:
- All the new CSS is in home.css, which loads on Home only. The footer 44px rule and the legacy-leak block are scoped to body.home. The header and footer partials are untouched.
- I grepped the preview /pricing/, /services/ and /about/, and none of these rules appear there.

Other checks:

- There are no changes to copy, section ids, data-cta values or dataLayer pushes beyond the lr-keys id. Business Analytics' PASS at ae871403 (including via "resize") still covers the tracking.

- Copywriter gives a PASS at this head.

Non-blocking:

text:

On correctness, dropping local("Arial") should still leave the fallback active on Mac and Windows. Chromium, Firefox and WebKit match local() against a font's full name or its PostScript name, and Arial's PostScript name on both Mac and Windows is ArialMT. Linux keeps Liberation Sans and Arimo.

One note on the PR body: "Chrome and Firefox never match local(\"Arial\")" is only true on Linux. On Mac and Windows they match it by full name. That doesn't affect this change.

pr_title: Fonts: metric-matched fallback for Instrument Serif
text:
**Code Review: APPROVED with conditions** at 1d99bceaa9e2b2983d57715bdaa905eb879143dc

Requested 9:44 AM PT Oct 18. Verdict 9:50 AM PT Oct 18.

**What changed:** a new italic `Instrument Serif Fallback` family, as two @font-face rules, in both `src/home.css` and `src/pricing.css`. One rule covers Gelasio and Georgia Italic at 80.32%, the other Times New Roman and Liberation Serif Italic at 91.22%. Three serif stacks are widened: `--pr-font-serif` in the :root tokens, `body.home --pr-font-serif`, and `body.pricing-h --ph-serif`. CSS only, with no markup, copy, id, data-cta or dataLayer changes, so no BA or CRO ping is needed and house rules don't come into play.

**Checked**
- No `local("Arial")` in either new face, which matches the #110 decision.
- The values are identical in home.css and pricing.css.
- The stack order is Instrument Serif, then the fallback face, then the named system serifs, then generic `serif`, so the real webfont still wins whenever it loads.
- `font-display:swap` is fine on local() faces.
- The PR body's numbers show Home at 360 going from one extra line with fonts blocked to the same 6 lines, across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
- CI passed. Strings, logos, hooks: success. Build and grep _site: success. Browser checks: skipped, which is standard for this repo.

**Conditions**
1. **Rebase onto main at b58d1b53 (#110) or later.** The base here is 565f3e7, from before #110, and the diff context still shows `local("Arial")` in the Figtree Fallback lines. A three-way merge would probably keep #110's removal, since this PR doesn't touch those lines. Even so, CI at this head ran on pre-#110 CSS, and I want the sha that merges to be the one I reviewed. After the rebase, ping me with the new sha. I'll check mechanically that the diff is unchanged and that `rg 'local\("Arial"\)' src/` comes up empty.
2. QA's WebKit and Firefox recheck comes back clean at the rebased head.

**Non-blocking notes**
- The two `Instrument Serif Fallback` rules share family, style and weight, with no unicode-range. Engines don't merge those into one list: the later rule (Times/Liberation, 91.22%) is preferred and the earlier one is only a fallback when its local() fails, and engines differ on that. That explains why Firefox picks Liberation while Chromium and WebKit on this box pick Gelasio. Each face is calibrated to the font it actually loads, so the result is right either way. On Mac and Windows, Times New Roman Italic exists, so the 91.22% face should apply. A short comment saying the two-face fallthrough is intentional would help the next reader.
- In the first rule, `local("Georgia")` and `local("Gelasio")` resolve to the upright faces, which the browser would then slant synthetically. Their advances differ from the italic that 80.32% was measured against. That only happens when neither Times nor Liberation nor a real Georgia/Gelasio Italic is present, so it's low risk, but you could drop those two names.
- WebKit keeps a 10 to 17px residual gap on `/` with the same line count. That's acceptable for a fallback.
- `services-h.css` needs the same follow-up after #111 merges, as you noted.

Limit: this review covers the PR diff plus GitHub CI. I did no local _site build.

pr_title: Fonts: metric-matched fallback for Instrument Serif
text:
**Code Review: APPROVED with conditions** at bf62e765ff1ec6308ac52aa698ae108f11502d5b

Requested 11:44 AM PT Oct 18. Verdict 11:48 AM PT Oct 18.

This is an incremental review from 1f563088, one commit, 2 files.

**Head script in `base.njk`**
- **CSP**: it's an inline script, and `_headers` script-src already has `'unsafe-inline'`, which GTM needs too. So no CSP or `_headers` change is needed. It makes no network requests.
- **Order**: it sits after `{% block criticalCss %}`. That's where Home links `home.css` and Pricing links `pricing.css`, the two files that declare the family. A parser-inserted inline script waits for the stylesheets above it, so the face is declared when `document.fonts.load()` runs. Keep it above `extraStylesheet` and any future font-face CSS.
- **Render**: it doesn't block on the font load. The promise isn't awaited, and the `.catch` is a no-op. The stylesheets above already block render, so the script adds no render delay worth noting.
- **No JS or old browsers**: the feature check returns early, and without JS the page gets the 1f563088 behavior. Degrades cleanly.
- **Other pages**: the script runs on every page. Where the family isn't declared, `load()` resolves to an empty list rather than rejecting, so it's harmless. Nit, optional: the comment says those pages "reject the load", but they actually resolve empty.

**`src/redesign-fonts.css`**: DM Sans Fallback roman and italic each go from 2 rules (`local('Arial')`, then `local('Liberation Sans')`) to 1 rule with `local('ArialMT'), local('Liberation Sans'), local('Arimo')`. The descriptors are unchanged. This matches the Figtree precedent and closes the earlier follow-up. This file loads on every page, so QA should spot-check that DM Sans text doesn't shift.

Review standard: PR diff plus GitHub CI, no local _site build. I ran the behaviour checks in headless Chromium against a harness built from the post.njk script verbatim at 0a64742, plus the two focus CSS rules. I compared it with the a36d28f version under both reduced-motion settings.

Requested Oct 18 2026, 3:04 PM PT
Verdict Oct 18 2026, 3:06 PM PT

## CI on 0a64742
- Strings, logos, hooks: success (3:04 PM PT)
- Build and grep _site: success (3:04 PM PT)
- Browser checks: skipped (expected)

## 1. Scope matches the description
compare a36d28f...0a64742: ahead 1, behind 0, 2 files.
- src/_includes/post.njk (+19/-9). All changes are inside the TOC script. clearFragmentFocus and its blur are removed. On a load with a hash, the target is marked with data-frag if it is an H2. clearFrag() runs on the first keydown ({ once: true }) and on a TOC click. The TOC click handler now ignores modifier clicks (meta, ctrl, shift, alt) so new-tab and new-window still work. Otherwise it calls preventDefault, then clearFrag, then pushState (only when the hash differs), then scrollIntoView(), then focus({preventScroll:true}).
- src/blog-post.css (+1/-0): adds `body.bpp h2[data-frag]:focus{outline:none}`.
Nothing else changed. Everything in post.njk above the bodyEndScripts block is byte-identical to a36d28f.

## 2. Headless Chromium results
a. Deep link (#s3): the heading scrolls into place (top 24px, which is the scroll-margin-top). Focus stays on the heading, which has data-frag and no outline. The next Tab goes to the first link after the heading. With a36d28f, focus was on body and the next Tab went to the same link.
b. Any first keydown removes data-frag. A lone Shift press leaves focus on the heading and the 3px solid ring appears. The heading is tabindex=-1, so it is not in the tab order: Tab then Shift+Tab goes to the previous section's link, not the heading. This is the same as a36d28f.
c. TOC click:
- The hash updates through pushState and adds exactly one history entry per new section.
- Back goes to the previous section with scroll restored. Back again goes to the page with no hash at scrollY 0. Forward returns to the section.
- With reduced motion the scroll is instant (the heading is at 24px 60ms after the click). With no-preference it is smooth, because scrollIntoView() with no options follows the CSS scroll-behavior rule.
- Focus lands on the heading. With the keyboard (Tab then Enter), :focus-visible is true and the 3px solid ring shows, and the next Tab goes to that section's link. With a mouse click there is no ring.
d. As expected, pushState fires no hashchange and :target does not update on a TOC click. Back and Forward do fire hashchange and popstate, and they update :target. Nothing depends on hashchange: no listener exists in script.js or post.njk. The only :target rule is `.menu-panel:target`, which applies to #mobile-menu on load. script.js revealHash() reads the hash only on load. A native anchor click at a36d28f never re-ran it either, so this is not a regression. Clicking the same TOC link twice more adds no history entries, because the `location.hash !== "#" + id` guard prevents it.
e. No page errors or console errors in any run.
f. The new rule only matches a focused h2 that has data-frag. At most one heading is marked, only the landed H2, and the mark is removed on the first keydown. Keyboard users therefore always see the ring once they interact, and no other element loses its outline. The existing `h2[tabindex="-1"]:focus:not(:focus-visible)` rule is unchanged. All links tested kept the 3px solid ring. WCAG 2.4.7 is met.

## 3. Invariants
- script.js and evaluate-boxed-cta.njk are not in the diff.
- In post.njk, data-cta* attributes, the Apply link text and the JSON-LD are unchanged (the JSON-LD is byte-identical to a36d28f).
- There is still exactly one `{% block themeColor %}`.
- No em dashes, en dashes or other Unicode dashes in any added line.
Tracking is unchanged, so BA's PASS carries forward.

## Nits (not blocking)
- Any keydown clears the mark, including a lone modifier or a copy shortcut, so the heading ring can appear without focus moving. This is the conservative choice for 2.4.7.
- Back and Forward restore scroll but do not move focus or re-mark the heading. The browser's native behaviour at a36d28f was the same.

text:
CHANGES REQUESTED

Requested Oct 18 2026, 2:46 PM PT. Verdict Oct 18 2026, 2:54 PM PT.
Review standard: PR diff plus GitHub CI, no local _site build. (A local build of main e3b286b and this head 2f82592 was also diffed, as supplementary evidence only.)
Head reviewed: 2f825926f23eb0be2481e6907ddcf6d698731129

CI on head: Strings, logos, hooks: success. Build and grep _site: success. Browser checks: skipped (normal).

## Must-fix

1. Instrument Serif Fallback no longer matches the #113 values, which must be preserved exactly.
   - Gelasio/Georgia face: main has size-adjust 80.32%, ascent 123.26%, descent 38.60%. font-faces.css has 75.73%, 130.74%, 40.94%.
   - Times/Liberation Italic face: main has 91.22%, 108.53%, 33.98%. font-faces.css has 86%, 115.11%, 36.04%.
   - Both are the #113 numbers multiplied by about 0.943. The PR body says these "stay 75.73 and 86", but that is only true against this PR's first commit. Against main they are a retune that was not called out.
   - The Times face src also gained local("Liberation Serif"), local("Times New Roman"). Those are upright family names inside an italic face. Where the italic names miss (the WebKit case the comment describes), this face now resolves to upright Times or Liberation with italic metrics instead of falling through to the Gelasio face. That is a behavior change from #113 too.
   - Fix: restore both faces to the exact #113 src lists and metrics, keeping the order (Gelasio/Georgia first, Times/Liberation Italic last). If the retune is wanted, it needs its own PR with Evan's sign-off on new known-correct values.
2. DM Sans Fallback changed without being documented. Main redesign-fonts.css has 106.70% / 92.97% / 29.05% (roman) and 106.84% / 92.85% / 29.01% (italic). font-faces.css has 103.35% / 95.99% / 29.99% and 103.48% / 95.86% / 29.95%, about 3.1% narrower, and that applies on every page. The PR body says DM Sans "stays 103.35 and 103.48", which again is only true against commit 1. Either restore the main values or add the measurements that justify the change (engines, widths, line counts) to the PR body.
3. After 1 and 2, update the "What changed" section so each metric is stated against main, not against the previous commit on this branch.

## Check results

1. Faces moved into font-faces.css (22 faces, no duplicates in any built page):
   - Figtree webfont 400/500/600 and Instrument Serif italic webfont: identical src and unicode-range. Fraunces, DM Sans, IBM Plex Mono webfonts: identical.
   - Figtree Fallback: retuned on purpose (this is the reflow fix). 400: 102.84 to 100.74, 500: 103.82 to 103.40, 600: 105.10 to 102.21. Ascent and descent rescaled to match. src is still local("ArialMT"),local("Liberation Sans"),local("Arimo"). Accepted as the improvement this PR is for.
   - Fraunces Fallback: all six faces scaled by 1.04, ascent and descent divided by 1.04. Arithmetic checks out. Documented with measurements. Accepted as an improvement, with the stated gaps at case-studies 360 and scorecard 390.
   - Instrument Serif Fallback: changed, see must-fix 1. No optional upright Liberation Serif face (allowed, it is optional). Note #118 does have one at scorecard-h.css line 11 and loses it when lines 4 to 13 go.
   - DM Sans Fallback: changed, see must-fix 2.
   - No local("Arial") anywhere in src.
2. Coverage and timing: base.njk links font-faces.css after site-kit.css and before redesign-fonts.css, foundation-coexist.css and page CSS. The bundle inlines it into the single head style block on every built page: Home, Services hub and all three service pages, Case Studies hub and all three case studies, About, Apply, Contact, Pricing, Scorecard, Author, blog posts, blog listing and pages 2+, blog categories, Privacy, Terms, 404. All show the same 22 faces. The bundle asserts in .eleventy.js now require font-faces.css on every page type. Inline in head, so no extra request and no late face swap from a stylesheet load.
3. ASSET_VERSIONS, passthrough, bundle-order assert and _headers (/font-faces.css, public, max-age=31536000, immutable, same as the other CSS) are all present and correct.
4. Head script: 402 B of JS, 419 B with the tag (matches the claim). Guarded by `if (!document.fonts || !document.fonts.load) return;`, each load has .catch, so no errors when the API is missing or a family is undeclared. It is a superset of the #113 script: 'italic 400 48px "Instrument Serif Fallback"' is still the first spec, and the script is in the same place (after criticalCss), after the inline style that declares the faces. CSP script-src uses 'unsafe-inline' with no hashes or nonces, so no violation. For reference if CSP moves to hashes later: sha256-B8ThSi9ZptuRYiMIpsFMBiglFfP+QlSW6EcCvRijrVs=
5. Copy and tracking: no changes. Visible text, data-cta, data-cta-location, id values and dataLayer are identical on every built page. script.js is not touched.
6. Build diff (main vs head): the only HTML differences are the inline CSS (face placement and metrics) and the head script. Outside @font-face, the only CSS change is the Services --pr-font-serif stack, which now includes "Instrument Serif Fallback" and matches the house stack exactly. Services pages had no Instrument Serif Fallback faces on main, so they gain them here (intended).
7. House rules: no em or en dashes in any added line.

## Nits

- src/_data/fontDisplay.js is not referenced by any template. Remove it, or use it.
- In .eleventy.js the check `heroDisplay !== "swap" && heroDisplay !== "optional"` can never fire, because the regex only captures those two words. A typo like `fallback` silently builds as swap. Match `hero-font-display:\s*(\w+)` and then validate.
- The font-faces.css header comment says faces must be dropped from scorecard-h.css and blog-post.css. Good. Please keep that note until #118 and #121 have landed.

## Unicode-range layering (read from font-faces.css)

- Order per family: webfont, then main's exact faces with no unicode-range, then the tuned faces limited to the webfont's range. Within a family, later faces take precedence for the characters they cover. Covered characters get the tuned face. Everything else falls back to main's face. The main layer has no range, so no character can fall through both. Names and descriptors are consistent: 35 faces per page, no duplicates.
  - Figtree: 3 webfont, 3 main, 3 tuned.
  - Instrument Serif: 1 webfont, then main Gelasio, main Times Italic, tuned Gelasio, tuned Times. The #113 order is kept in both layers.
  - Fraunces: 2 webfont, 6 main, 6 tuned.
  - DM Sans: 2 webfont, 2 main, 2 tuned.
  - IBM Plex Mono: 1 webfont.
- I checked the ranges against the real webfont cmaps from the preview.
  - Fraunces and DM Sans ranges match their cmaps exactly (136 and 138 codepoints).
  - Figtree and Instrument Serif use Google's broad latin range (387 codepoints), but the subset fonts hold 222 and 206.
- Every non-ASCII character the site renders: ©, ·, ×, U+2011, the curly quotes, …, ›, ←, →, ↓.
  - Each is either in the webfont, or outside the tuned range so main's face serves it.
  - → is outside Figtree, so Home gets main's metrics. › is outside DM Sans, so case studies get main's metrics. This matches Web Dev's 0.00px claim.
  - The only character that's in range but missing from the font is U+2011 for Figtree and Instrument Serif. Its one use is on Scorecard, which is DM Sans, so main's face serves it there.
- The two extra fonts.load calls with "\u2192" and "\u203A" warm main's Figtree and DM Sans layers for those glyphs. That's correct.

- Scoping:

  - The face is only used by body.services-h.page-website-build .tA h1 em, inside a container query (.tA content box 323 to 333px, which is viewports 407 to 417).
  - min-height is 3lh from 323 to 332px.

- Load: the @font-face lives in services-h.css, so it's declared on all 4 services pages (36 faces) and nowhere else. The other 3 pages never use it; it's only touched by the head script's fonts.load, which is a local font and costs no network. On non-services pages that load finds nothing and doesn't error.

- container-type: inline-size on .tA: the loaded layout matches main in Chromium at 360, 390, 407, 412, 417, 430, 768, 1024 and 1440 (same .tA and h1 boxes, same document height).

## Sans sources, uniqueness, loading, head script, CSP

- All 10 Figtree and DM Sans fallback faces use local("ArialMT"),local("Liberation Sans"),local("Arimo"). local("Arial") appears only inside comments in src and nowhere in the built _site.

- Head script:
  - 624 B with the tag. It's still guarded by `if (!document.fonts || !document.fonts.load) return;` and every load has .catch.
  - The #113 line 'italic 400 48px "Instrument Serif Fallback"' is still first. The script is still after criticalCss.
  - CSP is unchanged ('unsafe-inline', no hashes or nonces), so there's no violation.

## Copy, tracking, build diff, house rules

- Visible text, data-cta, data-cta-location, ids and dataLayer are identical on every built page. script.js is not touched. BA review not needed.
- Built HTML differs from main only in the inline font CSS, the head script, and the page-website-build body class on that page. Outside @font-face, the only CSS changes are on the services pages: the --pr-font-serif stack (from the earlier commits) and the website-build container rules.
- No em or en dashes in any added line, including docs/font-fallback/measurements.md and the PR body.

## Spot-check: preview vs live (live matches main)

Fonts were delayed 320ms; h1 lines are shown first paint to loaded. CLS is Chromium only, from this box's Chromium (Web Dev's "rounded" mode). Firefox and WebKit don't report layout shifts, so for those I give line counts only.

- Home 768: main 3 to 2, CLS 0.087. PR 2 to 2, CLS 0.023. Firefox 2 to 2 and WebKit 2 to 2 on the PR; on main, WebKit is 3 to 2.

Its src is local("Arial"), local("Helvetica Neue"), local("Helvetica"), local("Liberation Sans"), local("Noto Sans"), local("Roboto"), which breaks the never-local("Arial") rule. ## 2. Default rendering (passes)
Widths tested: 390, 545, 548, 550, 553, 555, 556, 558, 560, 563, 565, 700, 768, 860, 861, 1000 and 1440, with Figtree loaded and with the fonts blocked.
- No horizontal scroll at any width.
- No chip text overflows its pill.
- No title is clipped in the default rendering. The three capped Paid Acquisition titles render on their full loaded line count (feature h2 at 2 lines, two cards at 1 line). Their full text stays in the DOM (72, 63 and 61 characters).
- No page errors.

## 3. CLS (fixed in default rendering)
Test: the woff2 files were delayed 2.5s to force a font swap, at 545 to 565, 700, 860, 900 and 1000.
- c900c7b: CLS up to 0.25 at 545 to 565 on every page. Chip rows changed between the loaded and fallback fonts (paid-acquisition at 548: 3 rows vs 2; seo-local-search at 545: 2 rows vs 3).
- 15b4ad2: maximum CLS 0.0123 (/blog/ at 1000). Everything else is at or below 0.01, and the chip row count is identical in both fonts at every width.
The Motion CLS issue is fixed for default text settings.

## Blocking: WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing regression
Test: the standard 1.4.12 override (line-height 1.5, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em) on the Paid Acquisition page, compared with c900c7b under the same override.
1. Fixed chip widths with `overflow:visible` let label text spill out of the pills and overlap the next chip, across 545 to 1000. At 560 and 768, all five category chips overflow (for example Conversion & Infrastructure 211/197px, Content & AI Search 159/151px). At 900, four chips overflow. c900c7b has no chip overflow at any of these widths under the same override.
2. The `max-height` + `overflow:hidden` caps cut the three Paid Acquisition titles in half at 545 to 565. At 560: feature h2 scrollHeight 126 vs clientHeight 62, cards 48 vs 22. The feature heading shows one and a half lines, and the rest of the title is unreadable. c900c7b had 1 clipped heading at this width under the override; this head has 4, so the 3 capped titles are new. Text-only zoom (Safari and Firefox) would clip these the same way.
So the titles are readable and the DOM text is intact only at default text settings. This is an AA regression that c900c7b did not have.

Suggested fixes (any one that keeps CLS at 0.0123 or lower):
- Address the root cause with a metric-matched fallback @font-face for Figtree (size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override, line-gap-override). With that, the fallback wraps like Figtree, and the per-chip widths and title caps can be dropped.
- Or use `min-width` instead of `width` on the chips, drop `overflow:visible`, and replace the title caps with a `min-height` reservation or a font-metric fix instead of clipping.
After the fix, the 1.4.12 override should show no chip overflow and no clipped titles at 545 to 1000.

- The added comment still contains reviewer process notes: "PR #123 fix-cls: chip-row font-swap CLS (head c900c7b). Append after the fix-must block." Please trim it to describe the rule only. Keep the useful line "Chip widths must be remeasured if a category is added or renamed or the chip font size changes" if the widths stay.
- The caps use `nth-child(4)`, `nth-of-type(3)` and `.bi-feature` on the Paid Acquisition page, so they target post positions rather than specific posts. Publishing a new Paid Acquisition post would move the caps onto different titles.

text:
CHANGES REQUESTED

Re-review of 0bad970 (0bad97099ae5e610ef5c0437f2cfe797092f7b4c) against my APPROVED with conditions review 5565323614 at 813f137. compare 813f137...0bad970: ahead 3 (b27e4e0, df0e5a7, 0bad970), behind 0.

Review standard: PR diff plus GitHub CI, no local _site build. I ran the runtime checks in headless Chromium against the [preview host] previews for 0bad970 and 813f137. For the fallback tests, a fontconfig blocked the box's system Figtree, DM Sans, Fraunces, Instrument Serif and Instrument Sans, and the woff2 files were blocked or delayed 2.5s.

Requested Oct 20 2026, 10:32 PM PT
Verdict Oct 20 2026, 10:38 PM PT

## 8. CI on 0bad970
- Strings, logos, hooks: success (10:30 PM PT)
- Build and grep _site: success (10:30 PM PT)
- Browser checks: skipped (expected)

## 1. Diff
- .eleventy.js: utility.css is added to the blog-post `banned` list.
- 404.njk and legal.njk: themeColor changed to #ece6e8. legal.njk now includes bp-toc.njk in bodyEndScripts.
- New src/_includes/bp-toc.njk: the TOC script, shared by the posts and the legal pages. It binds both the rail and the phone list, adds tabindex=-1 at runtime only where it is missing, and closes the phone details when a link is picked. The data-frag, pushState and focus logic is the same as #121 at 0a64742.
- post.njk: the inline TOC script is replaced with that include. This changes #121's file; see item 11.
- utility.css (+628/-5):
  - Transitions moved to the base state, with transition:none under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and data-motion=off.
  - Apply hover changed to #8f3520.
  - R1 to R4.
  - Five fallback faces: Legal Measure, Legal Body 400 and 500, Legal Score, Legal Web.
  - Two .bp-stand em min-heights.
  - About 150 per-width min-height rules.

## 2. Fallback faces (pass)
All five new @font-face rules use only `src: local("ArialMT"), local("Liberation Sans"), local("Arimo")` with font-display: swap. None uses local("Arial"), and no italic faces were added. Nit: the shared body stack still names the Arial family directly (`Figtree, "Figtree Fallback", Arial, ...`). That is a font-family name, not a local() source, and it predates this PR.

## 3. Fallback CLS, clipping and min-height reserves
Widths tested: 360, 375, 390, 414, 768 and 1440 on /404.html, /privacy/ and /terms/.
- CLS with a 2.5s font delay: worst 0.0148 (/privacy/ at 360), then 0.007 (/404.html at 1440). Everything else is at or below 0.001. Pass.
- No horizontal scroll and no clipped text, with fonts loaded or blocked. No page errors.
- **Blocking: the reserves over-reserve once Figtree loads.** I measured each min-height box with Figtree loaded against its natural height, which the 'min-height' comment says should match. Many rules hold the taller fallback height, which leaves about one empty line (30px) under the paragraph on the loaded font. Examples:
  - /terms/ 390: p:nth-child(16) min 647px vs 617px natural (+30).
  - /terms/ 360: 254 vs 224 and 311 vs 280.
  - /terms/ 375 and 414: 226 vs 196.
  - /privacy/ 360: five boxes each +30 (170 vs 140, 86 vs 56, 114 vs 84, and others).
  - /privacy/ 375: 254 vs 224. /privacy/ 390: 142 vs 112. /privacy/ 414: 170 vs 140 and 198 vs 168.
  - /privacy/ 1440: the rail TOC link reserves 59px vs 38px.
  So most visitors, who get Figtree, see stray blank lines in the legal body on phones. The .bp-stand em reserves are fine with Figtree loaded; /terms/ 390 only adds +25px while on the fallback font.
- **Blocking: maintainability.** About 150 rules key on 1 to 15px width bands, `nth-child` positions and fixed px heights, for example `@media (min-width:340px) and (max-width:340px) { #pv-body .bp-prose > ul:nth-child(7) > li:nth-child(4) { min-height:170px } }`. Any copy edit, added paragraph, font-size change or new legal section silently moves or invalidates them. They also add about 20KB to each utility page's inlined CSS (Privacy 91.6KB to 112.6KB). In #123 we moved away from position-based holds for the same reason.
  Suggested fix: drop the range-reserve block and depend on the metric-matched faces (Legal Measure, Legal Body, Legal Score, Legal Web), which already show the right approach. Tune the shared body fallback's size-adjust for the legal prose so the line counts match, rather than reserving per box. If a few boxes still differ, use em-based reserves at the Figtree line count, not px at the fallback count. The CLS target is under 0.1, and this page is a long text document. A one-line rewrap at a few phone widths is likely well under 0.1 without any reserves, so please measure that before adding holds.

## 4. TOC include
- Desktop: `<nav class="bp-toc" aria-label="On this page">` is a labelled nav landmark. All 10 anchors resolve on Privacy and on Terms.
- Keyboard activation sets the hash, focuses the heading with the :focus-visible ring, and lands it at 48px.
- Phone (390): the phone `.bp-toc` closes the details after a pick.
- Posts: the TOC still has 8 links, with no JS errors.
- **Condition:** on phones the desktop nav is display:none, and the visible list is a `div.bp-toc` inside `details.ut-tocm`, so there is no nav landmark on phones. Wrap the details in a `<nav aria-label="On this page">`, or make that div a nav with a label. This markup predates this commit, so it is not a regression, but it should be fixed in this PR.

## 5. Hover contrast and motion (pass)
- Hover background #8f3520 with #fff text measures 7.78:1, above 4.5:1.
- With reduced motion set to reduce, the Apply and arrow transitions compute to none and the arrow transform is none. With no-preference they run at 160ms with translateX(3px).
- The .ut-chev transition is also set to none under reduce and data-motion=off.

## 6. Copy and posts (pass)
- The rendered main text is byte-identical to the 813f137 preview on /404.html, /privacy/, /terms/ and a sample post. SHA-1 prefixes: 404 71614d0772, privacy 0030de51f1, terms ca6e406558.
- No content source files changed.
- The blog-post build guard now bans utility.css, and Build and grep _site passed. The sample post requests no utility.css and contains no ut- selectors.

## 7. Tracking hooks (pass, no new BA PASS needed)
- On /404.html, /privacy/, /terms/ and the sample post, the sets of data-cta*, id and href attributes and the dataLayer snippets are identical to 813f137.
- bp-toc.njk only adds a runtime tabindex and pushState, and neither is a tracking hook.
- BA's PASS at 813f137 carries forward.

## 9. House rules (pass)
- No em or en dashes in added lines or rendered main text.
- No [former agency name] and no mailing address.
- Response time reads "1-2 business days" everywhere.
- No aggregateRating or Review markup.

## 10. Hex case (pass)
The #ECE6E8 nit is fixed (#ece6e8 in 404.njk and legal.njk). No uppercase hex remains in utility.css. The new hover is #8f3520.

## 11. Conflicts
- #124 targets cursor/blog-post-redesign. GitHub reports it mergeable and clean against that branch.
- **#121:** this PR rewrites post.njk's bodyEndScripts into bp-toc.njk. Any further #121 change to the TOC script must be made in bp-toc.njk, and the two copies must not drift. #121 should merge first and #124 should rebase.
- **#122:**
  - .eleventy.js: #124 shrinks `contentPages` to `["contact/index.html"]`, and #122 edits the `required` list inside the same contentPages branch (adding font-faces.css next to kit-page.css). This will conflict textually.
  - kit-page.css: after #124, 404, Privacy and Terms no longer get kit-page.css, so any #122 kit-page.css fixes for those pages will not reach them.
  - #122's font-faces.css should be checked against the new Legal faces.
  - Both PRs also add entries to `src/_headers`.
- **#125** overlaps on .eleventy.js (it adds footer.css plus a required-footer.css guard), src/404.njk, src/privacy.njk, src/terms.njk, src/_includes/post.njk and src/_headers. Recheck footer tracking and the post.njk bodyEndScripts after the rebase.
- **#126** overlaps on .eleventy.js (ASSET_VERSIONS and passthrough for menu-mc.css) and src/_headers. These are adjacent lines, so expect trivial conflicts.

## Conditions (carried over, apply once the blockers are fixed)
1. Retarget to main after #121 merges, and rebase.
2. If PM counts this as a redesign page, Evan's before/after screenshots are needed.
3. QA after merge.
New condition: add the phone TOC nav landmark (item 4).

CHANGES REQUESTED

Delta re-gate 77ea5bd...c1150c2 (1 commit).

Request time: Oct 21 2026 12:26 AM PT
Verdict time: Oct 21 2026 12:35 AM PT
Review standard: PR diff plus GitHub CI, no local _site build (plus preview browser checks)

**Scope: OK.** Only src/script.js changed (+28/-3). It touches no data-cta, data-cta-location or dataLayer push, and no bx-apply link. No hooks changed.

**BLOCKING: the scroll tracker is an rAF loop that runs all the time.**
- `watchScroll` starts with `requestAnimationFrame` when the script runs, then calls `requestAnimationFrame(watchScroll)` again every frame with no condition. Nothing ever cancels it: there is no handle and no cancelAnimationFrame.
- It runs on every page that has the menu, all the time. That includes desktop widths where the toggle is hidden, while the menu is closed, and while it is open (open only skips the body of the loop, not the next frame request).
- Preview check, Chromium, menu closed, idle: about 60 rAF callbacks per second at both 390 and 1280 (120 and 121 in 2 s). The page can never go fully idle, which costs battery on mobile.
- Per frame it reads scrollY and classList and calls performance.now(). Nothing big is allocated per frame, but the cost is constant.
- Fix: don't poll at all. Record the last nonzero scrollY in a passive `scroll` listener, and also on `pointerdown` and on `keydown` Enter/Space on the toggle. Those fire before the scroll-into-view and click happen, so they also cover WebKit. If you keep rAF, start it only on toggle pointerdown/focus, stop it after the open or after the 700 ms window, and cancel it on close.

**Non-blocking (post-launch list)**
1. The commit says the restore on close uses `scrollTo`. That code is not in this delta, so I assume it already existed. In the preview it works: 1500 → open (body top -1500px, no visible jump) → Escape → scrollY 1500.
2. The 700 ms staleness window in `readScroll` is a magic number. If the user scrolls up to the very top and opens within 700 ms, it restores to the old position. Rare and minor.

The patch is append-only CSS, so this matches the PR's cascade position.

1. Diff (main b3df851...5b76b44, 1 commit, src/scorecard-h.css +28/-2)
   - Only @font-face and font-family. A new "Figtree Optional" 400 face (font-display: optional, the same pricing-figtree-400.woff2) is applied to .sc-intro .lede, .sc-intro-points li and .sc-intro-meta in viewport-width bands. The Points Wide band is extended from 1017 to 1016.

2. Loaded layout: pixel-identical to main (full page, bbox none, same height) at 390, 414, 768 and 1440 in Chromium default, Chromium hinting-none and WebKit.
3. CLS sweep: incomplete, about 37% done. 3,078 of 8,262 loads covered widths 320 to about 580. Spike widths 391, 419-428 and 518-527 are covered; 1016-1028, 1241 and everything above about 580 are not, because the main preview stalled.
   - Chromium default and hinting-none, normal / delayed / staggered loads: PR max 0.0004, main max up to 0.0246. 0 cells over main+0.01.
   - WebKit normal and delayed: PR max 0.0002, 0 fails.
   - **WebKit staggered: 4 cells over main+0.01.** 388/389/390 read 0.025 on the PR vs 0 on main. 423 reads 0.0278 on the PR in 3 of 3 runs vs 0 on main in 3 of 3.    - Line counts match loaded. 390: lede 6, points 2/2/2, meta 2. 1440: lede 4, points 2/2/2, meta 1. Heights are identical (149/48/72 at 390; 114/53/65 at 1440).

## #125 follow-up: /contact/ WebKit delayed 320 (0.0317)
- Moving elements: hero `.ct-intro .lede`, the `application` link and `.ct-quiet` move up 47-48px at about 1.9-2.1s, when Figtree swaps in. Cause: #ct-h1 "Get in touch." goes from 96px (2 lines, fallback) to 49px (1 line). The footer is not involved: its top is 2020px at 320, far below the 900px viewport.
- PR vs main CSS: the only additions are footer-scoped (footer.footer.fx.fb2 rules and 3 Wordmark/Name fallback faces). No hero rule changed. Same font preloads, same H1 stack (Figtree, Contact H1 Sans, Figtree Fallback...).
- The same trace on main shows the identical move: H1 96->49 and lede 252->205 at 1899ms.
- WebKit sweep, 320-440 every 1px, 3 repeats, delayed and normal:
  - The direct lede-move tracker gives the same counts on PR and main: -47px in 9 delayed loads each, all at 320-322.
  - Max emulated CLS: PR 0.0317 vs main 0.0316, delayed.
  - The 3 flagged cells (320-322) read 0.030-0.032 on PR in 3/3 runs, and 0 / 0 / 0.031 on main. Main moves the same 47px in all 3 runs, so main's 0s are missed frames in the rAF emulator, not real differences.
  - Normal loads: PR max 0 vs main max 0.0087. 0 cells worse.
- Verdict: measurement artifact. The shift is pre-existing on main (#117 contact hero) and not caused by #125. No fix needed in #125. #125 at 41a2155 is CLEAR.

All of it is the site header and footer. `<main>` content matches section by section.

**Remaining computed-style differences.** There are 5 to 6 per width, and none of them change the render:

- 0 elements below 0.99 effective opacity, on load or after a full scroll, at 1440 and 390, in JS motion, reduced motion and JS off.

**One filled button per fold:**
- Main holds 2 filled buttons, the hero Apply and the close Apply, and they are never in the same half-viewport window.
- No bordered buttons.
- The fold script also counts the site-wide skip link, which only shows on focus. Same as main.

**Events:**
- 9 `<details>` FAQs, 0 open on load.
- `faq_toggle` pushes `{item, state}` on open and close.
- Hero Apply pushes `cta_click {cta_location:'pr-hero', cta_label:'Start with the Growth Blueprint', cta_destination:'apply', cta:'hero_apply'}`.
- Close Apply pushes `cta_location:'pr-final'`.
- `nav_menu_toggle` is as described in the table above.

**Focus rings.** Checked on painted pixels, not just computed styles:
- Every focus stop in main paints a 3px ring with a 3px offset.
- The ring is cobalt on the page, white and yellow surfaces, and white inside the cobalt and black cards. The hero Apply ring is white on cobalt, 7.15:1.
- Screenshots: `round2/focus-1440-*.png`, `focus-390-*.png` and `focus-scorecard-1440.png`.

**Tap targets:** everything in main is at least 44px. FAQ summaries are 66 to 91px. The 3 inline answer links are exempt. Only the site-wide skip link is under 44 (40px), unchanged from main.

**Contrast:** 0 AA failures at 1440 and 390. The lowest pair is #dfe4ff on cobalt at 5.68.

**Copy:**
- **86 of 86** required strings are present word for word in `<main>`.
- The 8 document-mock strings are absent.
- The capacity sentence pair appears once.
- 0 banned hits in visible text, attributes or raw HTML: em dash, en dash, [former agency name], core access, 48-hour, 1/one business day, SYS-, vetted, [employer].

**Metadata and JSON-LD:**
- Title, description, canonical, og and twitter tags are byte-identical to main.
- JSON-LD is identical to main. The FAQPage has 9 of 9 questions and answers matching the visible text.

**Console:** 0 errors and 0 warnings on /pricing/. The only failed requests are `google-analytics.com/g/collect`, aborted in the sandbox.

**Regression:**
- Home, /services/ and /about/ at 1440 and 390, head against main, full page: **0 changed pixels**, with identical document heights (12463/20300, 6713/9464 and 4536/6689) and identical section heights.
- The HTML is identical apart from the `script.js?v=` hash.

1. **Dead selector.** `.ph-id .ph-ck,.ph-act{margin-top:18px}` still names `.ph-act`, which no longer exists. Change it to `.ph-id .ph-ck{margin-top:18px}`.

The commit title says "short-phone hero", but no rule targets it; only the stacked spacing changed. Leave it unless Evan wants Apply visible on 667px-tall screens.
3. **JSON-LD `OfferCatalog` wording** ("we'd" against "we would"). Unchanged from main. Fix it in a copy PR.
4. **Naming (Web Design side).** The build pack's tokens use `--pr-`, the build uses `--ph-`. I can rename the pack to `--ph-` if wanted.

## Hub hero Apply at 375x667: which figure is right

**409/465 (top/bottom) is correct for a true 375 CSS-px viewport.** I re-measured with:
- DPR 1, 2 and 3, with and without mobile/touch emulation.
- At DOMContentLoaded, after `document.fonts.ready`, and with webfonts blocked.
- After a reload with scroll restoration from scrollY 3000.

The real header is 68px and the short-phone media query matches. Every run gave 409/465.

456/512 comes from a layout that is ≤370px wide. The H1's serif-italic line "service businesses" is 291px in a 295px box at 375, so it fits on 3 lines. At 371px or less it wraps to a 4th line, which pushes Apply down 47px to 456/512, the same value as the 340x720 run. A 375 window with a 15px classic scrollbar (360px layout), or a font raster about 4px wider, produces exactly that. So Web Dev's number is real for their environment but not for a 375 CSS-px phone. Two points:
- Apply is in the first screen either way (512 < 667).
- The H1 is only 4px from re-wrapping. If the team wants one number across environments, set `text-wrap:balance` on the hub H1 or trim its tracking slightly. This is optional, not a blocker.

## Must-fix R2-1: Website build hero sticker over the CTA

Web Motion's 390x640 finding is confirmed and is wider than reported. I ran a polygon sweep: the svg's rotated quad from its transform, SAT-tested against every CTA and text rect.

| Sweep | Cases | Overlaps |
|---|---|---|
| All 4 pages, widths 340 to 430, heights 568 to 800 | 256 | **56**, all on Website build: `stk-join-sticker-document` over `hero_apply` at every width 340 to 430 when height ≤760 (short-phone sticker rule) |
| All 4 pages, widths 431 to 1440, heights 800 and 900 | 112 | **8**, all on Website build at 861 to 1000: the 170px sticker's bottom (452) is below the button top (435) |

Hub, Blueprint and Google Ads have 0 overlaps. Website build is the only join where the button follows `.jl` directly: the hub has `ul.px` in between and the others have `dl.spec`. That leaves no spacer under the sticker.

**Paste-ready rule** (append to the end of `services-h.css`; also saved as `analysis/pr111/fix-must-r2.css`):

```css
@media (max-width:1000px){body.services-h .join .jl:has(+.btn){min-height:1.85em}}
```

Verified by injection on 798f7ce:
- **0 overlaps** in both sweeps (256 + 112 cases).
- The bbox gap is now 15px at short phones (button top 385 vs sticker 370) and 6px at 861 to 1000 (458 vs 452). The polygon gap is larger.
- Website build Apply moves down 20px (23px at 861 to 1000) and stays well inside the first screen: bottom 441 at 340 to 400 short phones, 394 at 430x760, 467 at 390x844, 514 at 861 to 1000.
- Hub, Blueprint and Google Ads are byte-unchanged with the rule applied (the selector does not match them). Desktop above 1000 is unchanged.
- Before/after shots: `r2/website-build-sticker-fix-390x640.png`, `r2/website-build-sticker-fix-861x900.png`.

## Pre-existing note (not caused by stickers, not new in this head)

At heights of 640 or less, the hero Apply falls below the first screen on:
- Growth Blueprint: bottom 656 at 340 to 375, 609 at 390 to 400.
- Google Ads: bottom 667 at 340, and 414 to 430 at 568.

These cases account for all 31 remaining "bad" rows in the short sweep, and none of them involves an overlap. It is the same on a103e57. If "Apply in the first screen" must hold down to 568, that needs a separate design decision on hero length. No rule is proposed here.

No fixes required.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Commit diff | Exactly one added line in `src/site-kit.css`, after the `nav.links a{…display:block…}` rule: `header.nav nav.links a{display:inline-flex;align-items:center}`. 1 file, +1/−0. |
| Label centring | On every page with desktop links (1001 to 1440), the label centre is within **0.5px** of the wordmark and Apply centres. On main, Home is the only page that was off: labels sat **14.5px high**. PR #112 corrects that to −0.5. Pricing, About, the blog post, the blog index and Case Studies were already at −0.5 and stay at −0.5. |
| Link boxes | Identical to main on every page and width. Home: Services 89.38×44, Case Studies 122.33×44. Other pages: 60.02×45 and 92.64×45. Only `display` changes (block → inline-flex). All other computed styles match. |

### Leak audit after the duplicate rules were removed
- These are still set by the base rules: `.sec` padding-bottom 0, `.cap` weight 400 in the sans, and the prose, role and close-lede measure (computed boxes identical to UB).
  - `body.author-h main p{max-width:none}` doesn't beat `.au-prose p` or `.au-role`, which are more specific.
  - The close lede computes to max-width 760px against UB's none. At 602px wide (306 on phones) the box is the same.

  - Font requests now start at about 137ms instead of about 208ms.

- **Figtree arrives, it isn't skipped.** I measured rendered H1 width against Figtree and the fallback, and the `em` against Instrument Serif and its fallback, 3s after load. At font delays of 0, 50, 100, 300 and 1500ms, the H1 renders in Figtree and the `em` in Instrument Serif in every case.

  - ink outside the cobalt newest-post card, as in UB
  - Nothing focusable sits on orange or on a cobalt surface.

## Must-fix

The paste-ready file is **`[local-path]`**. It replaces every `*Fallback` `@font-face` in `src/font-faces.css`, keeps the webfont rules as they are, and adds one media rule at the end of `src/redesign-fonts.css`.

1. **Loaded-state drift from glyphs outside the webfonts.**
   - Declare main's exact fallback faces first, with no `unicode-range`. These are the "legacy" layer: Figtree Fallback 102.84 / 103.82 / 105.10, Instrument Serif Fallback 80.32 / 91.22, Fraunces Fallback 94.28 / 105.07 and 89.55 / 101.70, DM Sans Fallback 106.70 / 106.84.
   - Then declare the new faces, each limited to its webfont's exact `unicode-range`.
   - Characters the webfont has use the new metrics. Characters it lacks (→, ›, and any future ones) render exactly as on main.
   - Verified: 0 px different from main on 39 page/width shots.
2. **website-build 414 and 415.**
   - `Figtree Fallback` 500: `size-adjust: 102.20%` (PR 103.40). Ascent 92.95 %, descent 24.46 %.
   - The Times / Liberation `Instrument Serif Fallback` rule: `size-adjust: 88.40%` (PR 86). Ascent 111.98 %, descent 35.07 %.
   - Figtree 400 and 600 and the Gelasio rule keep the PR's values.
   - These values sit inside a band that passes every requested Figtree cell in **both** rendering modes: Figtree 500 102.0 to 102.6, serif 88.2 to 88.5.
   - Result: website-build 414 and 415 go to 3/3 lines, wraps match, CLS 0 to 0.0002. Home 768, Services 390 and website-build 1440 still match.
3. **case-studies 360 and scorecard 390.**
   - Add a second family, `"Fraunces Fallback S"`, at **1.08×** the opsz-80 ratios: roman 113.47 % (Times/Liberation) and 101.82 % (Georgia), italic 109.84 % and 96.71 %.
   - Use it only where `h1-sub` is 36 px: `@media (max-width: 782.98px) { :root { --serif: "Fraunces", "Fraunces Fallback S", Georgia, "Times New Roman", "Liberation Serif", serif; } }`.
   - Desktop keeps the PR's 1.04× `Fraunces Fallback`, so scorecard 1440 stays matched.
   - Why it works: `--h1-sub` is `clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 64px)`, which is 36 px below 783 px. The webfont's opsz axis is wider at 36 px than at 64 px. That is the PR's own diagnosis; the media-scoped family resolves it without a shared number.
   - Result: case-studies 360 and scorecard 390 go to 3/3 lines, CLS 0.0001 to 0.0172.
   - In a wider sweep (9 Fraunces pages × 11 widths), Fraunces h1 failures drop from 5 (fractional) or 4 (integer-snapped) to 1: blog index 340, which also fails on the PR.
- **Untested:** the Georgia-sourced rules could not be exercised on this box because it has no Georgia. They are scaled by the same ratios as the Times/Liberation rules.

pr_title: Footer: FB ground close on every page
text:
proved Oct 18).
- Round 1 measurements were taken Oct 18 (3:44 to 4:01 PM PT). The run stopped in the usage outage before this file was written. This round (Oct 20, 8:15 to 8:58 PM PT) re-verifies the head, adds the font-swap CLS sweep and finishes the review.
- Rules held on every run: [local-path] Chromium; GA, GTM, Clarity, web3forms, hCaptcha and every other third party blocked (21,206 requests logged, 2,068 aborted, 0 analytics allowed); no form submitted; nothing posted on GitHub. Fallback runs hide the box's local Figtree and Instrument Serif.

Pages: Home, Services, a blog post (how-to-evaluate-a-marketing-agency), /blog/, 404, Privacy. Widths: 340, 390, 768, 1024, 1440 for geometry; 22 widths 340 to 1920 for scroll; every 1px at 357-363, 597-603, 857-863, 997-1003 and 1237-1243 for CLS. Modes: JS on, reduced motion, fonts held 1.5s, fonts blocked.

## Must-fix (all in fix-must.css, paste at the end of src/footer.css)

1. **New font-swap layout shift from the wordmark (fails QA's 0.01 line).** With fonts 1.5s late and the footer in view, the head's footer shifts 0.0104 to 0.0113 at 1237 to 1243px on Home, Services and /blog/: 19 of 105 sweep points, against 0.0001 to 0.0028 on base. Source is the two `.fx-name` spans. `Figtree Name Fallback` (size-adjust 88%) draws the name about 12% narrower than Figtree 600, so when Figtree lands the name widens and "Marketing" jumps sideways. It stays just under 0.01 at the other breakpoints (0.0084 to 0.0096), which is too close.
   Fix: a footer-only face `Figtree Footer Name` (ArialMT, Liberation Sans, Arimo; size-adjust 100%; ascent 95%, descent 25%, line gap 0, which is Figtree's own metrics) ahead of the 88% face. After the fix the worst footer CLS anywhere in the sweep is **0.0013**. With every web font blocked, the name still ends at least 17.1px inside the column at every width from 340 to 1920 (checked every 1px). The 88% face stays as the last net for devices without Arial-metric fonts.
2. **Legal links 1.1px narrow at every width.** The shared rule gives Privacy and Terms `letter-spacing: -0.01em`; FB has none. Terms sits 1.1px left on all 30 page and width pairs.
3. **Older pages (404, Privacy and the rest without Figtree yet) are 1.6px to 2.8px off FB.** They draw the footer in DM Sans at 18px with a taller line: note 2.8px wider, Start column 1.7px to 2px taller at 340 and 390, copyright 1.6px wider, wordmark 1.4px wider at 1440. Fix: footer font size and line height pinned to 16px / 1.55, and the Home Figtree files and fallback metrics loaded under **footer-only** family names. A plain `Figtree` face would also restyle the 404 header Apply button (my Oct 18 draft did this; it is replaced). Drop that block when #122 puts Figtree on every page.

**After injecting fix-must.css (local fonts hidden, so it behaves as on a real phone):**
- Every footer box is within 1px of FB at 340, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 on all six pages (max delta 0.0px).
- Footer heights equal FB: 914.1, 912.6, 849.5, 829.5 and 864.4px.
- Nothing above the footer moves: same footer top and same page height minus footer on all six pages; same fonts on every header and main element.
- No sideways scroll at 22 widths.
- The one pixel delta above the footer is the sticky Privacy table of contents in a full-page capture. Its link boxes are identical.

## Passes at head (no change needed)
- **Copy:** all 16 footer strings are word for word FB on all six pages, in FB order (Apply block, Explore, Start, wordmark with "Digital marketing since 2003.", legal row). No em or en dashes. "1-2" never breaks from 320 to 1920; it is wrapped in span.nw on /blog/ and unwrapped elsewhere, as the PR says.
- **Apply:** a quiet underlined text link to /apply/ on every page, never filled. No filled button inside the footer on any page. The fold above it keeps the page's own single filled CTA.
- **Scorecard:** a text link.
- **data-cta:** footer_apply, footer_scorecard and footer_contact on Home and Services only, unchanged from base.
- **Terra square:** not drawn (approved).
- **Contrast and taps:** lowest text contrast 6.22:1 (AA); every footer tap target at least 44px at 1440, 390 and 340.
- **Focus:** every footer link shows the 3px cobalt ring, offset 3px.
- **Scope:** header and menu pixels match base. Page height minus footer matches base within 0.8px on Home, Services, post and 404. Only the footer changed.
- **Fallback (fonts blocked):** no clipped text, no overflow, name inside the column at all widths.

## CLS sweep detail (fonts held 1.5s, local fonts hidden)
- 840 measured points across base, head and head plus fix-must, plus 77 repeats. Raw rows are in `analysis/pr125/cls-sweep-2026-10-20.json`.
- **New at head:** the wordmark shift above. Nothing else in the footer reaches 0.01.
- **Pre-existing, not this PR (flag to QA):**
  - The blog post sometimes shifts 0.2 to 0.9 when fonts land while scrolled to the bottom. The source is the FAQ section and the related list above the footer, moving the whole page. It shows on base in 25 of 77 runs and on head in 40 of 77 (the same intermittent event; the footer's own boxes do not move).
  - The 404 page shifts 0.016 to 0.035 on load from its h1 and header button. Base shows the same (0.0167 to 0.0355), and the same 0.0349 outlier appears on both base and head.

## Should-fix (non-blocking)
- I agree with the code review's must-fix that `Figtree Name Fallback` should use the house local() list (ArialMT, Liberation Sans, Arimo), not local("Arial"). That is outside this footer file; fix-must.css already follows the house list for its own faces.

### Round 4 addendum: wordmark fallback width (Code Review 5595106681), Oct 20 2026, 9:55 to 10:08 PM PT

**System Figtree is excluded from every measurement.** Every Round 1 to 4 geometry and CLS run, and every run below, launches Chromium with `FONTCONFIG_FILE=[local-path]`. That file rejects `/usr/share/fonts/truetype/sand-box/google/Figtree/*` and `.../Instrument Serif/*`. I checked this three ways:
- Under that config, `fc-match Figtree` returns Noto Sans.
- `fc-list` finds 0 Figtree or Instrument Serif files.
- Inside the browser, `new FontFace('x','local("Figtree"), local("Figtree SemiBold")').load()` fails ("not found").

The "fallback" runs abort every .woff/.woff2 request, so they show what a phone sees if Figtree never arrives. The "loaded" runs use the site's own Figtree files.

**Correction to the premise.** At 600px and below, the wordmark is two stacked lines (each span is `display:block`), not one. It is a single line only above 600px. Measured by text extent at the 9d1c78d head (Home and 404, 210 widths from 340 to 1920), the 100% fallback is 4.1% to 5.7% narrower than Figtree at every width, desktop included. It is not 2.6% narrower at 768 and 1440. That works out to 13 to 16px on phones and 19 to 36px on desktop.

**Why the width and the CLS pull apart on desktop.** On the single line, the 100% Liberation face draws "[the agency]" at exactly Figtree's width (408.9px at 1243). Only "Marketing" is narrower. When Figtree lands, "Marketing" starts 7px further left and widens by 35px. If you scale the fallback up to match the total width, "[the agency]" becomes too wide (419.9px at 102.3%). Then "Marketing" jumps 19px left on the swap instead of 7px, and footer CLS goes up. One size-adjust cannot match both words. Compensating ascent and descent for the size-adjust (tested) fixed a 3px vertical move but not the horizontal one.

**Width change on swap, in px (Figtree minus fallback; positive means it widens), with the CLS result from 156 runs each against the same 156 main runs:**

| Option | 360 | 390 | 768 | 1000 | 1001 | 1440 | Fallback inside column (worst gap) | Footer CLS max | Max residual over main | Cells over main + 0.0013 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: 100% (head 9d1c78d) | +13 | +16 | +19 | +27 | +27 | +27 | yes (-19.2px) | 0.0088 | 0.0013 | 0 |
| B: 105% mobile / 102.7% desktop (CR) | -4 | 0 | -5 | -7 | -7 | 0 | yes (-1.9px) | 0.0089 | 0.0038 | 48 |
| C: 105% / 102.3%, metrics compensated | -4 | 0 | -5 | +2 | +2 | 0 | yes (-3.2px) | 0.0087 | 0.0035 | 46 |
| **D: 105% at 600px and below, 100% above (recommended)** | **-4** | **0** | +19 | +27 | +27 | +27 | yes (-5.1px) | 0.0087 | **0.0013** | **0** |

- In all options the wordmark never wraps (the same line count in fallback and loaded at all 210 widths) and never overflows. The wordmark height is identical, so the footer height holds.
- Liberation hinting snaps glyph advances to whole pixels, so the deltas move about ±4px between neighbouring widths. Mean |delta| from 340 to 600: A 20.3px, B/C/D 2.6px. Mean |delta| above 600: A and D 24.9px, B 2.5px, C 1.6px.
- The 0.0087 in C and D is Services at 390. It comes from `section.close` above the footer and is also on main (residual 0.0000).

**Recommendation: D, the per-width split.**
- On phones it removes the swap reflow: 0 to 4px against 13 to 29px today. Mobile CLS stays at main's level, because both lines are left-aligned blocks and only their right edges move.
- On desktop it keeps today's 100% face. That is the only desktop value that passes the CLS residual bar: B and C each leave 46 to 48 cells over main + 0.0013, up to 0.0038.
- If PM prefers the smallest desktop reflow over the residual bar, C's desktop face (102.3%, ascent 92.86%, descent 24.44%) gets the reflow to about 2px. It costs up to 0.0035 CLS, still under 0.01.

**Paste-ready CSS for D** (also at `analysis/pr125/wordmark-split.css`). Add it after the existing Figtree Wordmark Fallback face in `src/footer.css`. It does not change desktop.
```css
@font-face{font-family:"Figtree Wordmark Fallback Mobile";font-style:normal;font-weight:600;font-display:swap;src:local("ArialMT"),local("Liberation Sans"),local("Arimo");size-adjust:105%;ascent-override:90.48%;descent-override:23.81%;line-gap-override:0%}
@media (max-width: 600px){footer.footer.fx.fb2 .fx-name{font-family:Figtree,"Figtree Wordmark Fallback Mobile","Figtree Wordmark Fallback","Figtree Name Fallback",system-ui,sans-serif}}
```
This does not change the Round 4 verdict (CLEAR at 9d1c78d). D is an optional improvement for CR's condition. If it lands, the change is footer-only: re-run the mobile widths and the CLS sweep on the new head.

## The named asks (all pass)

The toggle sits at x 684 on live, main and the PR alike, and the mock's 23px comes from its own hc.css shell. Matching the mock here would put the Close tile 17px off the toggle it replaces.
- **Open and closed:** the toggle opens the sheet. Close, Escape, a link tap and resizing past 1000 all close it. Focus returns to the toggle, and scroll position is kept (900 → 900).
- **Focus trap:** focus lands on Close when the menu opens. 12 Tab presses and then 12 Shift+Tab presses all stayed inside the dialog. role=dialog, aria-modal, aria-controls and aria-expanded are all correct.

### The live phrases you asked about (flag only)

- **"10 to 15%": absent.** The [client 3] page now reads "Roughly 10 to 20%" in the glance figure and in the Year 2 row ("Direct online bookings and sales are roughly 10 to 20% of Rich's total business."). The PR says 10 to 20% is the approved draft figure. [client 1] and [client 5] have no percentage.
- **"most business closes by phone": present in reworded form** in the Year 2 row: "Most bookings still come by phone and text, and the sites are what drive those calls and texts." Also: "without relying exclusively on phone calls and word of mouth" (twice), "its organic presence still brings in a lot of calls, inquiries, and bookings", "Two sites ... driving calls, texts, and bookings". This clashes with the no-calls positioning (no call CTA is shown). Flag for Evan, not a defect.
- [client 1] and [client 5]: no phone wording. [client 5] keeps "Ranked among Southern California's top patio installation companies" (unverifiable superlative, live copy): flag for Evan.
- **Phone or URL signage on photos: none.** The case pages carry no photos, only logos. I viewed the [client 3] logo (green "JUNK" wordmark), the [client 4] logo (name only) and the [client 5] hub photo (patio cover, no text, no signage). The [client 1] logo is a gray wordmark. None contain a phone number or URL. Text-only illustrative mocks do show URL strings (`junkcontrol.com › services › las-vegas`, `[client-2-slug].com`, and the map query "patio builders coachella valley"), which are typed text, not photo signage, and are labelled illustrative.

### Hub

- Taller than the mockup by +285px at 1440 (PR: 2644 vs 2342; my render is 2654 vs 2369 after the `fdc5a12` margin fixes). The reasons are as declared: the 199-word [client 4] content, the "Who this is for." block (43px H2 plus lede), and three illustrative mocks that stay with captions. I judge this acceptable. The H1's two lines add 65px of it (below).
- Mock maps: star rows and review counts are gone. Kept: rank numerals 1, 2, 3 and invented competitor names ("[demo label]", "[demo label]"), plus "Licensed and insured junk removal ..." in the [client 3] search mock. The numerals imply "[client 5] ranks #1", which reads as an outcome metric. SHOULD-FIX for Evan (PR open question 2): drop the numerals, or keep them under the Illustrative caption.
- [client 1] logo panel is linen with a 1px line border and 8px radius. The logo is a gray wordmark (#4D4D4D): 2.16:1 on ink, 7.18:1 on linen. Acceptable (declared and sensible); the other three stay ink.
- Hub LCP is 3.2s in the PR's Lighthouse run (above the 3.0s note). Cards and mocks are below the fold, so this comes from the H1 (see below).

### Hub H1: the LCP hack (judgment)

Web Dev's stated reason: the hub H1 must be the LCP element (`lcp-element.mjs`). So they added `#cs-h1{max-width:11em}` (two lines on desktop), `.cs-card .case-media{aspect-ratio:16/9}` (shorter photo), and `font-size:44px;line-height:1.08;max-width:none` at 760 and under.
- 44px is above the Home H1 floor (`--h1` clamp starts at 42px) and above every other sub-page (36px). It makes the 390 H1 three lines and 143px tall (mockup 73px, 70px more before the lede). The two-line desktop H1 adds 65px.
- I tested the check: with the H1 at the kit's 36px, the lede paragraph becomes the LCP element at 390 and at 412 (and already is at 360 even with 44px). So the 44px is what makes the check pass, and it still fails at 360 on the page as built. It is a Web Dev gate, not a kit requirement (same finding as PR61).
- Judgment: **SHOULD-FIX, strongly recommended; not a block by itself** (2px over Home's floor is far smaller than PR61's 58px; the 11em measure is acceptable). Exact fix below. The proper long-term fix is the check (accept a text element as LCP).

### Detail pages: other diffs vs template (all acceptable)

- Results list text 18px vs mock 19px on [client 3] (mock draws two lists at 19). Missing `<b>` highlight in one row. Trivial.
- [client 3] hero adds the search-result mock and the "At a glance" figures use new labels ("Roughly 10 to 20%"); fine.
- [client 4] section: 199 words, H2 "How [client 4] launched from ..." runs four lines at 1440 (207px). Acceptable (approved content).
- The 36px detail H1 at 390 plus 16px margin matches the mockup; hero heights differ only by the added mocks and longer ledes (e.g. [client 3] hero 720 vs 491 at 390).
- LCP on detail pages: [client 3] H1 at 1440 and lede at 390; [client 1] the result line at 1440 and lede at 390; [client 5] lede at both. Not in the H1 opt-in; same advice as above.

### JSON-LD

| Page | Types | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Hub | CollectionPage + ItemList (3 ListItems) + BreadcrumbList | match |
| [client 3] | Article (headline updated, `dateModified` 2026-10-01, `about` = Organization "[client 3]" and "[client 4]" by name only), BreadcrumbList; no Person, address or sameAs | match. Open: Article `description` still describes the single-brand story (PR open question 5) |
| [client 1], [client 5] | Article + BreadcrumbList (`dateModified` 2026-09-29) | match |
| Any | No Review, AggregateRating, ratingValue, reviewCount or telephone | match |

No scenario eyebrow on detail pages, no Common Thread block, no per-card Apply buttons on the hub, no pricing ghost button, no "Same playbook" strip, one mid-story text link only. Hub keeps the Durability / Rescue / Expansion badges.

| Scorecard results | Only the lead-gated results state is reachable without submitting the web3forms lead form (not submitted: it posts to a third party). Gate shows score "53 / 100", tier heading, blurred rows, 1 h1, 1 filled button, no horizontal scroll at all 6 widths. The unlocked full results were not exercised. |

## Must-fix (blocks launch)
None.

## Should-fix (later)
- **S1. Case-studies hub, empty space in the cards at 1001px and up.** `a.card{display:block}` beats `.cs-card{display:flex}` (specificity 0,1,1 vs 0,1,0), so `.cs-more{margin-top:auto}` never pins the link and the grid stretches all three cards to the tallest ([client 3] 1012px at 1440): [client 5] ends with 422px of blank card (527px at 1024), [client 1] 137px. Fix options, both tested at 1440/1024/768/390 with no horizontal scroll: (a) `@media (min-width:1001px){.cs-grid{align-items:start}}` gives cards of 1012/900/614px at 1440, ragged bottoms but no blank card space; (b) `a.card.cs-card{display:flex}` moves the link to the bottom with the gap between the stat and the link (437px for [client 5]), not better. Option (a) is the cleaner one. Mobile and tablet are fine.
- **S2. Mobile menu loses scroll position (also on base `13f68d5`, not new in this PR).** Opening the menu jumps the page to the top (scrollY 1500 becomes 0) and closing leaves it at the top. Cause: `html.menu-open{overflow:hidden}` while `body{overflow-x:hidden}` makes the body its own overflow container. Fix: `body{overflow-x:clip}` (as `body.home` already does) or lock with `position:fixed` and restore `scrollY` on close in `script.js`.
- **S3. "Since 2003" outside the footer.** Evan's rule says only About under the H1 and the footer. Author page `.au-role` (under its h1) has it and About's is in the founder section, not under the h1. Mockup `blog-author.html` also has it in the bio. Confirm the rule with Evan; the PR check only warns on this.
- **S4. Ticker Play does not visibly resume until focus leaves the button (Chrome).** Clicking the label focuses the checkbox, and `html.js .lr:focus-within .lr-track{animation-play-state:paused}` keeps it paused (still paused after 2.7s; resumes on blur). Fix: scope it, for example `html.js .lr-viewport:focus-within .lr-track` (keeps keyboard and hover pausing on the logo list, not on the button).
- Minor, not worth a ticket: desktop Privacy and Terms sidebar TOC links are 35px high (mobile ones are 44); footer Blog link 34px wide.

## Key numbers
- 63 pages in the sitemap crawled by HTML: footer line 63/63, 1 h1 on 63/63, 0 banned strings, 0 phone or address. 22 page views x 6 widths in the browser: 0 horizontal scroll, 0 site console errors, 0 broken images, 0 missing focus indicators (except third-party iframes), 0 fold with 2 filled buttons.
- PR changed files (62): 33 blog posts and llms files, plus `src/script.js` (+9/-183), `src/kit-content-pages.css` (+14), `src/blog.css` (-11), `src/case-studies.njk` (-11, mock map figure removed from the [client 5] card), `src/foundation-coexist.css` (+4/-4), `src/_includes/method-diagram.njk` (removed), footer, pricing, apply, scorecard, services, About, author, check scripts.

## Files
- Screenshots: `[local-path]` (`shots/<page>-<width>-fold1.jpg` and `-full.jpg` for 22 pages x 6 widths, `menu-*-open.png`, `menu-nojs-*.png`, `toc-*-open.png`, `cs-hub-*-full.png`, `cs-hub-*-withfix.png`, `apply-selects-*.png`, `sc-gate-*.png`, `ticker-*.png`). Raw results: `audit-<width>.json`, scripts `audit.py` and `i*.py`.
- Eyeballed myself: menu open at 390, Home 390 fold, case-studies hub 1440 and 390, Apply selects at 390, Scorecard gate at 390, author page at 390. The rest are checked by computed styles and measurements, not by eye.
- Method: Playwright (`[local-path]`) against the preview; the PR, commit list and file list were read through `cursor-github` (read only). The [preview host] preview blocks the default Python user agent (403), so the HTML crawl used a curl user agent.

pr_title: Fix contact captcha scale, service overflow, and menu focus scroll
text:
ds wrapper right.
  - 349 and below uses scale .8 (iframe right 280.6, inside the wrapper at every width from 320 to 349; slack is only 0.4px at 320).
  - 350 is the tightest case at scale .9: iframe right 310.80 against wrapper right 311.0, so 0.2px of slack. It does not clip.
  - 400 is scaled .9; 401 is unscaled (303px iframe in a 323px wrapper).
- documentElement.scrollWidth equals clientWidth at all widths. Form fields and the card are unchanged horizontally (field right edge is at most 351 at 390, within the card).
- Layout: the transformed wrapper keeps its unscaled layout height (83px), and the 14px bottom margin replaces 22px. The gap between the widget and the next field is 49px at 360/375/390 on head (base 57px). Whole-page height at 390 is 8px shorter (2495 against 2503), which is the margin change only. Header and footer crops are pixel-identical to base.
- With the `.invalid` state forced, the error text sits inside the wrapper at 340, 360, and 390 (wrapper right edge is at or inside the card inner edge, and no horizontal scroll). The error text is scaled with the wrapper, so it renders at about 13.5px at .9 and 12px at .8 (see note 1).
- 768 and 1440: whole-page pixel diff against base is empty (iframes hidden for the diff). CSS computed transform is none and widths are identical.
- Console errors on /contact/ at all widths: 0 on head and 0 on base.

## (2) /services/* pages: overflow clip (hub, google-ads-management, growth-blueprint, website-build)
- Computed body overflow-x: head = clip, base = visible. html is visible on both. The four pages are the only ones changed; every other paper page already had clip on base.
- At 1440, 1024, 768, 390, 360 on all four pages: scrollWidth minus clientWidth = 0 on head, and also 0 on base. Trying `scrollTo(200, y)` leaves scrollX at 0. A broader sweep of 16 widths from 320 to 1920 with scrolling through each page also gave 0 on head and on base. Note: base already had no measurable overflow at these widths in this headless run, so this PR is a protective fix (it hides a latent overflow) and is not visibly "fixing" something here.
- Visual diff vs base: full-page screenshots, 4 pages x 5 widths = 20 pairs, all **pixel-identical** (diff bbox None; page heights identical).
- Sticky and header: there are zero `position:sticky` elements on the four services pages (both base and head); the header is `position:relative` on both (site design). `overflow-x:clip` does not create a scroll container, so sticky ancestors would still work. Other pages with sticky (/privacy/ `.lg-toc` top:96px) are unaffected and unchanged. After scrolling to 1200, the header offset is identical to base (-1200).
- The `@supports not (overflow: clip)` fallback uses hidden. This only matters on browsers without clip (Safari older than 16), and no sticky elements exist on these pages, so there is no risk.
- Console errors: 0 on head and 0 on base for all 40 loads.

## (3) Mobile menu close on a scrolled page
Test: touch emulation at 390x844 and 360x740, Home, Pricing, and Services hub, JS on. scrollTo 1500, open the menu, close three ways, check scrollY, then tap a same-page link. Because the header is not sticky, the toggle is off-screen at 1500, so the toggle was clicked via JS.
- Scroll lock while open: scrollY stays 1500 while the menu is open (html.menu-open sets overflow:hidden, and the overlay is position:fixed), on both base and head.
- Result after close (before = 1500 each time):

| path | base: close button / Esc / toggle | head: close button / Esc / toggle |
|---|---|---|
| Home 390 | 30 / 30 / 39 | **1500 / 1500 / 1500** |
| Home 360 | 30 / 39 / 39 | **1500 / 1500 / 1500** |
| Pricing 390, 360 | 0 / 0 / 0 | **1500 / 1500 / 1500** |
| Services hub 390, 360 | 0 / 0 / 0 | **1500 / 1500 / 1500** |

  - Focus returns to the menu toggle (`BUTTON.menu-btn`), aria-expanded goes back to false, and the menu closes, on head and base.
  - The base jump was caused by `btn.focus()` scrolling the off-screen toggle into view. The head fix removes it. This matches the diff.
- Link tap on the same page (menu link to the current path): this triggers a full navigation, and the page reloads at scrollY 0 on both base and head (`expect_navigation` fired). That is normal browser behaviour for same-URL navigation and is not caused by menu focus handling. The menu links on these pages contain no in-page anchors, and the close-by-link path (`c(false)`) never focused the toggle anyway. If "no jump" was expected for a same-page link, it needs a separate change (note 2).
- Console errors: 0 on head and base.

## (4) Regression: Home, Services hub, Apply, Contact
Full-page screenshots (reduced-motion, animations off, hCaptcha iframe hidden) base vs head at 1440, 768, and 390:
- Home, Services hub, Apply: 9 of 9 pixel-identical (diff bbox None).
- Contact at 1440 and 768: identical. Contact at 390: header and footer crops are pixel-identical. The only change is the captcha spacing (page 8px shorter; margin 22px to 14px).
- Header and footer heights are the same on head and base for all four pages.
- No horizontal scroll (scrollWidth minus clientWidth = 0) on any page or width.
- Console errors on head: 0 on all four pages at all three widths (base also 0).

## Notes (non-blocking)
1. At under 350px the error text "Complete the captcha, then submit again." scales to 12px visual (15px x .8), and about 13.5px at 350 to 400px. It was 13.5px on base too, and is only for the invalid state, but is below the site's usual 15px minimum. Optional fix: counter-scale the `.h-captcha-err` font-size (about 18.75px under 349px and 16.7px from 350 to 400px) or accept it.
2. The same-page link tap loads at top because it is a real navigation (not caused by this PR; base is identical). Only fix if that case is wanted.
Also: slack at 350px is 0.2px (iframe right 310.80 against wrapper right 311.0). It does not clip, but a 1px change in card padding would. If padding at about 350px ever changes, re-test.

pr_title: Motion: real Pause button, working kill switches, Pricing plate, reveals on inner pages, motion cleanups
text:
ip.
- Keyboard: Tab from `.lr-viewport` lands on the button. The ring is `3px solid rgb(143,53,32)` with a 3px offset and a 999px radius, and it matches `:focus-visible`. Screenshot: shots/home-strip-focus-1440.png.
- Overlap: none. The button is beside the viewport (flex order viewport, then button) with a 16px gap at 1440 and 10px at 390. The button's box does not intersect any logo clipped to the viewport.
